title: 15th Sitting of First session of 2026

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/15/1/2026).

Question from Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development Dr Abdulla Muttalib: the President announced Chinese assistance to upgrade Malé's roads to a modern standard; when will practical work start, how is it planned to finish, and how will it be done to limit the impact on Malé's extremely congested traffic flow?

Question from Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister Dr Abdulla Muttalib: Malé City Council says residency registration cannot be issued under the rental agreements now being signed with Fahi Dhiriulhun Corporation; if so, what happens to the residency status of the people living in those flats?

Question from Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister Dr Abdulla Muttalib: under the "Gedhoruveriya" scheme, has any relief been decided on the advance payments due for the 4,000 flats being built through Fahi Dhiriulhun Corporation?

From the Speaker's desk: the President's request for Parliament's approval to amend Schedule 1 of the Drugs Act (Law No. 17/2011), under Article 3-4(c) of that Act, is sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

Unfinished business: debate continues on the resolution by Galolhu South MP Meekail Ahmed Naseem on Public Service Media discriminating between political parties, denying the Maldivian Democratic Party the chance to inform the public, and failing to ensure the editorial independence required by law.
Unfinished business: debate continues on the Bill to amend the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, submitted by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim.
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting opened with three housing and roads questions to the Housing Minister, sent a Drugs Act schedule amendment to committee, and continued debate on the PSM resolution and the Constitution amendment bill.
